# Gossip / Epidemic Protocols

## What is Gossip?

Gossip protocols are a family of **decentralized information dissemination** algorithms. Each node periodically exchanges state with a small, randomly chosen set of peers. Information spreads through the network like an epidemic — exponentially fast and resilient to failures.

```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ Traditional Consensus (Raft/Paxos)                       │
│                                                          │
│  Leader ──► Follower-1                                   │
│         ──► Follower-2       Centralized, strong consistency
│         ──► Follower-3       Leader bottleneck, 2N+1 faults
│                                                          │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│ Gossip (SWIM/HyParView)                                  │
│                                                          │
│  A ◄──► B ◄──► C       Decentralized, eventual consistency
│  │       │       │      O(log N) convergence, scalable
│  ▼       ▼       ▼      Any node can fail anytime
│  D ◄──► E ◄──► F                                         │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

## Core Properties

| Property | Value |
|---|---|
| **Convergence** | O(log N) rounds to propagate to all nodes |
| **Scalability** | Each node sends O(1) messages per round |
| **Resilience** | Tolerates arbitrary node failures |
| **Consistency** | Eventual (not strong — use Raft for strong) |
| **Overhead** | ~1-2 KB/s per node for membership gossip |
| **Typical interval** | 200ms-1s per gossip round |

## Gossip Protocol Families

```
Gossip Protocols
├── Membership (who is alive?)
│   ├── SWIM (Scalable Weakly-consistent Infection-style Membership)
│   ├── HyParView (Hybrid Partial View)
│   ├── SCAMP (Scalable Membership Protocol)
│   └── Cyclon
├── Dissemination (spread data)
│   ├── Anti-entropy (full state sync → eventual consistency)
│   ├── Rumor-mongering (push rumors until heard by K nodes)
│   └── Plumtree (eager push + lazy pull — epidemic broadcast trees)
├── Aggregation (compute global stats)
│   ├── Push-Sum
│   ├── Push-Pull Gossip Averaging
│   └── Flow-Join
└── Overlay Management (maintain topology)
    ├── T-Man (Topology Manager)
    └── Vicinity (proximity-aware)
```

## SWIM Protocol (Hashicorp Memberlist / Serf / Consul)

SWIM is the most widely deployed gossip membership protocol. Core idea:

```
Each node P runs two continuous processes:

1. PING-REQ: Pick random target Q, ping it
   ┌── If Q responds: success
   └── If Q doesn't respond after timeout:
       ├── Select K random nodes as intermediaries
       ├── Send PING-REQ(Q) to each intermediary
       ├── Intermediaries forward ping to Q
       └── If Q still doesn't respond: mark Q as SUSPECT

2. DISSEMINATION: Periodically send my membership list
   ├── Full state push (piggybacked on ping/ping-req)
   ├── Delta state: only changed entries since last round
   └── Gossip to random subset (fanout = 3)

State per node:
  [A: alive, n=5, t=1234]  ← incarnation number + timestamp
  [B: suspect, n=3, t=1200] ← suspected, may recover
  [C: dead, n=2, t=1100]    ← confirmed dead
```

### SWIM State Machine

```
                  timeout
    ALIVE ──────────────────► SUSPECT
      ▲                         │
      │ refute (higher n)       │ timeout (no refutation)
      │                         │
      └─────────────────────────▼
                              DEAD
```

### SWIM Key Parameters

| Parameter | Typical Value | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| Protocol period | 200ms | Faster detection vs overhead tradeoff |
| Ping timeout | 500ms-1s | Must be > RTT to avoid false positives |
| Indirect pings (K) | 3 | More = fewer false positives, more load |
| Suspicion timeout | 3-5s | Time a node stays SUSPECT before DEAD |
| Fanout | 3 | How many peers to gossip to per round |
| Message size | ~512 bytes | Per-gossip message overhead |

### SWIM in Rust (simplified)

```rust
use std::collections::HashMap;
use std::time::{Duration, Instant};
use tokio::sync::RwLock;

#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq)]
enum MemberState {
    Alive,
    Suspect,
    Dead,
}

#[derive(Clone, Debug)]
struct Member {
    addr: String,
    state: MemberState,
    incarnation: u64,  // monotonic counter
    last_seen: Instant,
}

struct SwimNode {
    members: Arc<RwLock<HashMap<String, Member>>>,
    myself: String,
    period: Duration,
    ping_timeout: Duration,
    k: usize,  // indirect ping count
}

impl SwimNode {
    async fn protocol_loop(&self) {
        let mut tick = tokio::time::interval(self.period);
        loop {
            tick.tick().await;
            let target = self.pick_random_member().await;
            match self.ping(&target).await {
                Ok(ack) => self.handle_ack(&target, ack).await,
                Err(_) => self.handle_timeout(&target).await,
            }
        }
    }

    async fn handle_timeout(&self, target: &str) {
        // Mark as suspect, not dead — give chance to refute
        self.update_member(target, MemberState::Suspect).await;
        
        // Indirect ping via K intermediaries
        let intermediaries = self.pick_random_members(self.k).await;
        let mut recovered = false;
        for proxy in &intermediaries {
            if self.ping_req(target, proxy).await.is_ok() {
                recovered = true;
                break;
            }
        }
        
        if !recovered {
            self.update_member(target, MemberState::Dead).await;
        }
    }

    async fn ping(&self, target: &str) -> Result<Ack, Error> {
        let conn = tokio::net::TcpStream::connect(target)
            .timeout(self.ping_timeout)
            .await??;
        // Send PING with my incarnation + membership digest
        Ok(Ack { incarnation: 42 })
    }
}
```

## HyParView (Hybrid Partial View)

Unlike SWIM's full membership, HyParView maintains two partial views:

```
Active View (small, ~log N)         Passive View (larger, ~N)
┌─────────────────────┐            ┌──────────────────────────┐
│ Direct connections   │◄── random ─│ Backup pool               │
│ Used for forwarding  │   shuffle  │ For replacing failed nodes│
│ Must stay connected  │            │ Periodically shuffled     │
│ Size: 5-10           │            │ Size: 30-100              │
└─────────────────────┘            └──────────────────────────┘
```

### HyParView Operations

```rust
struct HyParViewNode {
    active: Vec<PeerId>,      // size: ~log N
    passive: Vec<PeerId>,     // size: up to max_passive
    max_active: usize,        // typically 5-10
    max_passive: usize,       // typically 30-100
}

impl HyParViewNode {
    // When active peer fails: replace from passive
    fn handle_failure(&mut self, failed: PeerId) {
        self.active.retain(|p| *p != failed);
        if let Some(replacement) = self.passive.pop() {
            self.active.push(replacement);
        }
        // If passive empty, ask other active peers for candidates
    }

    // Shuffle: periodically exchange passive peers
    fn shuffle(&mut self) {
        let peer = pick_random(&self.active);
        let candidates = pick_random(&self.passive, 5);
        // Send candidates to peer, receive their candidates back
        // Merge into local passive, evict oldest if over capacity
    }
}
```

### HyParView vs SWIM

| Aspect | SWIM | HyParView |
|---|---|---|
| Membership knowledge | Full (everyone knows everyone) | Partial (O(log N) per node) |
| Scalability | ~10K nodes | ~100K+ nodes |
| Failure detection | Ping/Ping-Req indirect | TCP disconnect + gossip |
| Message overhead | O(1) per round | O(1) per round |
| Join | Need seed node | Need seed node |
| Best for | Small clusters, Consul/Serf | Large P2P, BitTorrent DHT |

## Epidemic Dissemination (Rumor Spreading)

Three classic strategies:

### 1. Anti-Entropy (full state reconciliation)

```
Node A: {a:1, b:2, c:3}
Node B: {a:1, c:4, d:5}

Round 1:
  A → B: {a:1, b:2, c:3}
  B → A: {a:1, c:4, d:5}
  
After merge (latest-write-wins):
  Both: {a:1, b:2, c:4, d:5}
```

### 2. Rumor Mongering (push)

```
When a node learns new info:
  1. Push to k random nodes (hot rumor → k=log N)
  2. Each recipient pushes to k random nodes
  3. Stops when enough nodes already know it

Termination: recipient says "already heard" → 
  P(keep pushing) decreases with each "already heard"
```

### 3. Plumtree (Epidemic Broadcast Trees)

```
Step 1: Eager Push — use gossip to build a spanning tree
Step 2: Lazy Pull  — missed messages repaired via gossip pull

Tree construction:
  Each node sends "I have msg M" to random subset.
  First message received → mark sender as tree parent.
  Subsequent copies → mark sender for repair (lazy push list).
```

## Failure Detection

### Simple Heartbeat

```
Every T seconds, node sends heartbeat.
If no heartbeat within T × timeout_factor → declared dead.

Problem: fixed threshold can't adapt to network conditions.
```

### Phi-Accrual Failure Detector (Akka, Cassandra)

```
Instead of yes/no, compute a suspicion LEVEL:

1. Maintain sliding window of heartbeat inter-arrival times
2. Fit to a distribution (normal or exponential)
3. φ = -log₁₀(P(arrival_time > current_delay))

Interpretation:
  φ = 1    → 10% chance it's a false positive
  φ = 2    → 1% chance
  φ = 3    → 0.1% chance
  φ = 8+   → essentially certain

Threshold: φ > 8 → suspect, take action (but allow recovery)
```

### Phi-Accrual in Rust

```rust
use std::collections::VecDeque;

struct PhiAccrualDetector {
    window: VecDeque<f64>,  // last N inter-arrival times (ms)
    window_size: usize,
    threshold: f64,          // typically 8.0
    last_heartbeat: Instant,
}

impl PhiAccrualDetector {
    fn phi(&self) -> f64 {
        if self.window.len() < 2 { return 0.0; }
        
        let mean = self.window.iter().sum::<f64>() / self.window.len() as f64;
        let variance = self.window.iter()
            .map(|x| (x - mean).powi(2))
            .sum::<f64>() / self.window.len() as f64;
        let std_dev = variance.sqrt().max(0.001);  // avoid div by zero
        
        let elapsed = self.last_heartbeat.elapsed().as_millis() as f64;
        let phi = (elapsed - mean) / std_dev;
        
        // Cumulative normal distribution approx
        -phi.log10()
    }

    fn is_suspect(&self) -> bool {
        self.phi() > self.threshold
    }

    fn heartbeat(&mut self) {
        let elapsed = self.last_heartbeat.elapsed().as_millis() as f64;
        self.window.push_back(elapsed);
        if self.window.len() > self.window_size {
            self.window.pop_front();
        }
        self.last_heartbeat = Instant::now();
    }
}
```

## CRDTs (Conflict-Free Replicated Data Types)

Gossip naturally pairs with CRDTs — data structures that converge automatically when merged, regardless of order.

| CRDT | Operation | Merge | Use |
|---|---|---|
| **G-Counter** | increment | max(elements) | Counting |
| **PN-Counter** | inc/dec | max(P), max(N) | Counting with decrement |
| **G-Set** | add | union | Membership set |
| **2P-Set** | add/remove | union(adds) \ union(removes) | Set with remove |
| **LWW-Register** | assign | max(timestamp) | Key-value store |
| **OR-Set** | add/remove | adds \ removes | Observed-remove set |
| **OR-Map** | nested | recursive merge | Dynamo-style DB |

### LWW-Register (Last-Write-Wins)

```rust
#[derive(Clone, Debug)]
struct LWWRegister<T> {
    value: T,
    timestamp: u64,
    node_id: u64,  // tiebreaker
}

impl<T: Clone> LWWRegister<T> {
    fn merge(&self, other: &Self) -> Self {
        if other.timestamp > self.timestamp 
           || (other.timestamp == self.timestamp && other.node_id > self.node_id) {
            other.clone()
        } else {
            self.clone()
        }
    }
}
```

### OR-Set (Observed-Remove Set)

```rust
// Each added element gets a unique tag. Remove only removes known tags.
use std::collections::{HashMap, HashSet};

struct ORSet<T: Eq + Hash> {
    elements: HashMap<T, HashSet<u64>>,  // element → {tags}
}

impl<T: Eq + Hash + Clone> ORSet<T> {
    fn add(&mut self, elem: T, tag: u64) {
        self.elements.entry(elem).or_default().insert(tag);
    }

    fn remove(&mut self, elem: T) -> Option<HashSet<u64>> {
        // Return all CURRENT tags so other replicas can remove them
        self.elements.remove(&elem)
    }

    fn merge(&mut self, other: &ORSet<T>) {
        for (elem, tags) in &other.elements {
            let entry = self.elements.entry(elem.clone()).or_default();
            entry.extend(tags);
        }
    }
}
```

## Gossip vs Consensus

| | Gossip | Raft/Paxos |
|---|---|---|
| **Consistency** | Eventual | Strong (linearizable) |
| **Throughput** | Very high | Leader bottleneck |
| **Latency** | Sub-second convergence | ~100ms per log entry |
| **Partition tolerance** | ✅ Always available | ⚠️ Majority required |
| **Membership** | Dynamic, any node can join | Fixed cluster, manual reconfig |
| **Use case** | Service discovery, config sync | Database replication, leader election |

### When to use Gossip:
- Cluster membership tracking (Consul, Serf)
- Configuration distribution (Dynamo, Riak)
- Failure detection (Cassandra)
- Overlay network maintenance (BitTorrent DHT)
- Vector clock reconciliation

### When to use Raft:
- Strongly consistent key-value store
- Distributed lock service
- Log replication (RDBMS)
- Leader election
- Configuration changes that must be atomic

## Real-World Systems

| System | Protocol | Use |
|---|---|---|
| **Cassandra** | Gossip + Phi-accrual | Cluster membership, failure detection |
| **DynamoDB** | Gossip + Merkle trees | Anti-entropy, hinted handoff |
| **Consul** | SWIM (Serf) | Service discovery, health checking |
| **Hashicorp Serf** | SWIM | Lightweight cluster membership |
| **Akka Cluster** | Gossip + Vector clocks | Actor cluster membership |
| **Riak** | Gossip + CRDTs | Distributed KV store |
| **CockroachDB** | Gossip + Raft | Hybrid: gossip for topology, raft for data |
| **BitTorrent DHT** | Kademlia + gossip | Peer discovery |
| **IPFS** | libp2p gossipsub | Pub/sub message dissemination |
| **Kubernetes** | etcd (Raft) | NOT gossip — strong consistency for cluster state |

## ANDL Relevance: Expert Node Cluster

For a distributed MoE inference cluster, gossip enables:

```
┌───────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ ANDL Coordinator                                       │
│                                                         │
│  Gossip Layer:                                          │
│  ├── Membership: which expert nodes are alive?          │
│  ├── Health: what's each node's load/VRAM/capability?   │
│  ├── Expert Placement: where is each expert currently?  │
│  └── Hot/Cold Rebalancing: redistribute experts         │
│                                                         │
│  Why gossip (not Raft)?                                 │
│  ├── No strong consistency needed for expert placement  │
│  ├── Nodes can fail independently (no majority needed)  │
│  ├── Eventually consistent expert routing table          │
│  └── Scales to 100+ expert nodes                        │
└───────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

### Hot/Cold Expert Rebalancing via Gossip

```
Phase 1: Each node periodically gossip its expert heat map
  Node A: "I have expert [5]: 1000 hits/sec (HOT)"
  Node B: "I have expert [5]: 10 hits/sec (COLD)"
         "I have expert [88]: 800 hits/sec (HOT)"
  Node C: "I have expert [88]: 2 hits/sec (COLD)"

Phase 2: Coordinator/Leader detects imbalance
  Expert 5: Node A HOT, Node B COLD → keep on A
  Expert 88: Node B HOT, Node C COLD → keep on B

Phase 3: Rebalance via expert weight transfer
  If Node D joins empty:
    Gossip to discover hottest experts not duplicated
    Node D requests "cold" copy from any node
    Promotes to HOT locally
```

## Pitfalls

1. **Message storms.** Fanout × gossip interval must be bounded. 10 nodes × 10 fanout × 100ms = 1000 msgs/s — fine. 1000 nodes × 50 fanout = 500K msgs/s — problematic.

2. **Split-brain in SWIM.** If a suspect node is alive but isolated, it selects a new incarnation and re-announces. All nodes must accept the higher incarnation number.

3. **Gossip doesn't replace consensus.** Don't use gossip for things that need atomicity (leader election, transaction commit). Pair gossip (membership) with Raft (data plane).

4. **Cold start.** New node needs at least one seed to bootstrap. If all seeds disappear, the cluster can't grow.

5. **Network partitions.** Gossip handles partitions gracefully (eventual consistency), but the application must handle stale data for up to seconds.

6. **CRDTs grow unboundedly.** OR-Set tags accumulate forever. Use tombstone garbage collection with a "sufficiently old" threshold.

## Refs

- [SWIM Paper](https://www.cs.cornell.edu/projects/Quicksilver/public_pdfs/SWIM.pdf) — original SWIM protocol
- [Lifeguard: SWIM with Noise](https://arxiv.org/abs/1707.00788) — improvements to SWIM
- [Hashicorp Memberlist](https://github.com/hashicorp/memberlist) — Go SWIM implementation
- [HyParView Paper](https://asc.di.fct.unl.pt/~jleitao/pdf/dsn07-leitao.pdf) — HyParView membership
- [Plumtree](https://www.gsd.inesc-id.pt/~ler/reports/jleitao09srds.pdf) — Epidemic broadcast trees
- [Phi-Accrual Detector](https://www.jaist.ac.jp/~defago/files/pdf/IS_RR_2004_010.pdf) — original paper
- [CRDTs](https://crdt.tech/) — comprehensive CRDT resource
- [Rust gossip libraries](https://crates.io/search?q=gossip) — crates.io

| Aspect | SWIM | HyParView |
|---|---|---|
| Membership knowledge | Full (everyone knows everyone) | Partial (O(log N) per node) |
| Scalability | ~10K nodes | ~100K+ nodes |
| Failure detection | Ping/Ping-Req indirect | TCP disconnect + gossip |
| Message overhead | O(1) per round | O(1) per round |
| Join | Need seed node | Need seed node |
| Best for | Small clusters, Consul/Serf | Large P2P, BitTorrent DHT |

## Epidemic Dissemination (Rumor Spreading)

Three classic strategies:

### 1. Anti-Entropy (full state reconciliation)

```
Node A: {a:1, b:2, c:3}
Node B: {a:1, c:4, d:5}

Round 1:
  A → B: {a:1, b:2, c:3}
  B → A: {a:1, c:4, d:5}
  
After merge (latest-write-wins):
  Both: {a:1, b:2, c:4, d:5}
```

### 2. Rumor Mongering (push)

```
When a node learns new info:
  1. Push to k random nodes (hot rumor → k=log N)
  2. Each recipient pushes to k random nodes
  3. Stops when enough nodes already know it

Termination: recipient says "already heard" → 
  P(keep pushing) decreases with each "already heard"
```

### 3. Plumtree (Epidemic Broadcast Trees)

```
Step 1: Eager Push — use gossip to build a spanning tree
Step 2: Lazy Pull  — missed messages repaired via gossip pull

Tree construction:
  Each node sends "I have msg M" to random subset.
  First message received → mark sender as tree parent.
  Subsequent copies → mark sender for repair (lazy push list).
```

## Failure Detection

### Simple Heartbeat

```
Every T seconds, node sends heartbeat.
If no heartbeat within T × timeout_factor → declared dead.

Problem: fixed threshold can't adapt to network conditions.
```

### Phi-Accrual Failure Detector (Akka, Cassandra)

```
Instead of yes/no, compute a suspicion LEVEL:

1. Maintain sliding window of heartbeat inter-arrival times
2. Fit to a distribution (normal or exponential)
3. φ = -log₁₀(P(arrival_time > current_delay))

Interpretation:
  φ = 1    → 10% chance it's a false positive
  φ = 2    → 1% chance
  φ = 3    → 0.1% chance
  φ = 8+   → essentially certain

Threshold: φ > 8 → suspect, take action (but allow recovery)
```

### Phi-Accrual in Rust

```rust
use std::collections::VecDeque;

struct PhiAccrualDetector {
    window: VecDeque<f64>,  // last N inter-arrival times (ms)
    window_size: usize,
    threshold: f64,          // typically 8.0
    last_heartbeat: Instant,
}

impl PhiAccrualDetector {
    fn phi(&self) -> f64 {
        if self.window.len() < 2 { return 0.0; }
        
        let mean = self.window.iter().sum::<f64>() / self.window.len() as f64;
        let variance = self.window.iter()
            .map(|x| (x - mean).powi(2))
            .sum::<f64>() / self.window.len() as f64;
        let std_dev = variance.sqrt().max(0.001);  // avoid div by zero
        
        let elapsed = self.last_heartbeat.elapsed().as_millis() as f64;
        let phi = (elapsed - mean) / std_dev;
        
        // Cumulative normal distribution approx
        -phi.log10()
    }

    fn is_suspect(&self) -> bool {
        self.phi() > self.threshold
    }

    fn heartbeat(&mut self) {
        let elapsed = self.last_heartbeat.elapsed().as_millis() as f64;
        self.window.push_back(elapsed);
        if self.window.len() > self.window_size {
            self.window.pop_front();
        }
        self.last_heartbeat = Instant::now();
    }
}
```

## CRDTs (Conflict-Free Replicated Data Types)

Gossip naturally pairs with CRDTs — data structures that converge automatically when merged, regardless of order.

| CRDT | Operation | Merge | Use |
|---|---|---|
| **G-Counter** | increment | max(elements) | Counting |
| **PN-Counter** | inc/dec | max(P), max(N) | Counting with decrement |
| **G-Set** | add | union | Membership set |
| **2P-Set** | add/remove | union(adds) \ union(removes) | Set with remove |
| **LWW-Register** | assign | max(timestamp) | Key-value store |
| **OR-Set** | add/remove | adds \ removes | Observed-remove set |
| **OR-Map** | nested | recursive merge | Dynamo-style DB |

### LWW-Register (Last-Write-Wins)

```rust
#[derive(Clone, Debug)]
struct LWWRegister<T> {
    value: T,
    timestamp: u64,
    node_id: u64,  // tiebreaker
}

impl<T: Clone> LWWRegister<T> {
    fn merge(&self, other: &Self) -> Self {
        if other.timestamp > self.timestamp 
           || (other.timestamp == self.timestamp && other.node_id > self.node_id) {
            other.clone()
        } else {
            self.clone()
        }
    }
}
```

### OR-Set (Observed-Remove Set)

```rust
// Each added element gets a unique tag. Remove only removes known tags.
use std::collections::{HashMap, HashSet};

struct ORSet<T: Eq + Hash> {
    elements: HashMap<T, HashSet<u64>>,  // element → {tags}
}

impl<T: Eq + Hash + Clone> ORSet<T> {
    fn add(&mut self, elem: T, tag: u64) {
        self.elements.entry(elem).or_default().insert(tag);
    }

    fn remove(&mut self, elem: T) -> Option<HashSet<u64>> {
        // Return all CURRENT tags so other replicas can remove them
        self.elements.remove(&elem)
    }

    fn merge(&mut self, other: &ORSet<T>) {
        for (elem, tags) in &other.elements {
            let entry = self.elements.entry(elem.clone()).or_default();
            entry.extend(tags);
        }
    }
}
```

## Gossip vs Consensus

| | Gossip | Raft/Paxos |
|---|---|---|
| **Consistency** | Eventual | Strong (linearizable) |
| **Throughput** | Very high | Leader bottleneck |
| **Latency** | Sub-second convergence | ~100ms per log entry |
| **Partition tolerance** | ✅ Always available | ⚠️ Majority required |
| **Membership** | Dynamic, any node can join | Fixed cluster, manual reconfig |
| **Use case** | Service discovery, config sync | Database replication, leader election |

### When to use Gossip:
- Cluster membership tracking (Consul, Serf)
- Configuration distribution (Dynamo, Riak)
- Failure detection (Cassandra)
- Overlay network maintenance (BitTorrent DHT)
- Vector clock reconciliation

### When to use Raft:
- Strongly consistent key-value store
- Distributed lock service
- Log replication (RDBMS)
- Leader election
- Configuration changes that must be atomic

## ANDL Relevance: Expert Node Cluster

For a distributed MoE inference cluster, gossip enables:

```
┌───────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ ANDL Coordinator                                       │
│                                                         │
│  Gossip Layer:                                          │
│  ├── Membership: which expert nodes are alive?          │
│  ├── Health: what's each node's load/VRAM/capability?   │
│  ├── Expert Placement: where is each expert currently?  │
│  └── Hot/Cold Rebalancing: redistribute experts         │
│                                                         │
│  Why gossip (not Raft)?                                 │
│  ├── No strong consistency needed for expert placement  │
│  ├── Nodes can fail independently (no majority needed)  │
│  ├── Eventually consistent expert routing table          │
│  └── Scales to 100+ expert nodes                        │
└───────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

### Hot/Cold Expert Rebalancing via Gossip

```
Phase 1: Each node periodically gossip its expert heat map
  Node A: "I have expert [5]: 1000 hits/sec (HOT)"
  Node B: "I have expert [5]: 10 hits/sec (COLD)"
         "I have expert [88]: 800 hits/sec (HOT)"
  Node C: "I have expert [88]: 2 hits/sec (COLD)"

Phase 2: Coordinator/Leader detects imbalance
  Expert 5: Node A HOT, Node B COLD → keep on A
  Expert 88: Node B HOT, Node C COLD → keep on B

Phase 3: Rebalance via expert weight transfer
  If Node D joins empty:
    Gossip to discover hottest experts not duplicated
    Node D requests "cold" copy from any node
    Promotes to HOT locally
```

## Pitfalls

1. **Message storms.** Fanout × gossip interval must be bounded. 10 nodes × 10 fanout × 100ms = 1000 msgs/s — fine. 1000 nodes × 50 fanout = 500K msgs/s — problematic.

2. **Split-brain in SWIM.** If a suspect node is alive but isolated, it selects a new incarnation and re-announces. All nodes must accept the higher incarnation number.

3. **Gossip doesn't replace consensus.** Don't use gossip for things that need atomicity (leader election, transaction commit). Pair gossip (membership) with Raft (data plane).

4. **Cold start.** New node needs at least one seed to bootstrap. If all seeds disappear, the cluster can't grow.

5. **Network partitions.** Gossip handles partitions gracefully (eventual consistency), but the application must handle stale data for up to seconds.

6. **CRDTs grow unboundedly.** OR-Set tags accumulate forever. Use tombstone garbage collection with a "sufficiently old" threshold.
